value.name: rabbi sings wedding song
value.description: Rabbi Bolensky emerges from behind the bower and sings as the wedding ceremony begins.
evidence: From behind the bower, RABBI BOLENSKY emerges, strumming his guitar and singing
Parsley sage, rosemary and thyme -- Remember me to one who lives there...

value.name: couple stands before altar
value.description: Howard and Marylin are revealed standing before the altar as the ceremony proceeds.
evidence: A pullback reveals Howard D. Doyle before the altar with Marylin.
He is in a tuxedo and yarmulke. She is dressed in a simple, Kennedy-type gown.

value.name: guests sit after song ends
value.description: When the song ends, the wedding guests settle into their seats.
evidence: The last arpeggiated chord rings out; birds tweet, everyone sits.

value.name: Miles notices Wrigley crying
value.description: As Miles and Wrigley sit down, Miles sees Wrigley sniffling and reacts with irritation.
evidence: As Miles and Wrigley seat themselves, Wrigley is sniffling. Miles is irritated.
MILES What the hell is wrong with you?

value.name: Wrigley explains ceremony moves him
value.description: Wrigley admits he cannot help getting emotional because the wedding feels optimistic to him.
evidence: WRIGLEY I can't help it. Even with the business we're in, I -- it gets me every time. It's so -- optimistic.

value.name: Miles questions wedding commitment
value.description: Miles asks whether Marylin is actually going through with the marriage, signaling his doubt about the union.
evidence: MILES Is she going through with it?

value.name: Wrigley implies marriage is nearly underway
value.description: Wrigley replies that if Marylin is backing out, she is doing so very late in the process.
evidence: WRIGLEY If she's not going through with it, she's cutting it awful close.

value.name: rabbi compares marriage to feast
value.description: Rabbi Bolensky delivers a metaphorical sermon describing marriage as a banquet with stages and courses.
evidence: Marriage is like a Great Feast.
The Early Years -- The First Course -- a carefully poached fish dish dependent on freshness and delicate handling.
Or perhaps a light pasta -- a tortellini stuffed with cheese and hope.
